statement: Let n = len(words). Define a pair (i,j) to be good iff 0 <= i < j < n and words[i] is both a prefix and a suffix of words[j], where a string a is a prefix of a string b iff len(a) <= len(b) and a[k] = b[k] for every 0 <= k < len(a), and a is a suffix of b iff len(a) <= len(b) and a[k] = b[len(b)-len(a)+k] for every 0 <= k < len(a). Whenever count_prefix_suffix_pairs(words) returns a result r, r equals the number of good pairs (i,j).
preconditions: words is a slice of byte vectors satisfying the problem constraints: 1 <= len(words) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), 1 <= len(words[i]) <= 100000 and every byte of words[i] is in 97..122; and sum_{i=0}^{len(words)-1} len(words[i]) <= 500000.
